newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD sell-off may be delayed until March.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD sell-off may be delayed until March.

text.p: The vice-president and privatization chief of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has confirmed the privatization of state mining giant CVRD may be delayed until March.
The initial sell-off of a 40-45 percent block of voting shares in Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) was expected to take place in February.

Jose Pio Borges said the BNDES was running a very tight schedule in allocating enough time to all interested investors to study the information on CVRD in the so-called Data Room at the BNDES building in Rio de Janeiro.

"Our objective (for the auction) is the second half of February. But, this is an ambitious objective," Borges said. "If we can't make the second half of February then it will be the first half of March, but definitely not later than the first quarter (of 1997)."

Borges said eight companies had prequalified to visit the Data Room, Brazil's Votorantim and CSN, South Africa's Anglo American Corp and Gencor Ltd, Canada's Noranda, Korea's Hyundai Corp and Japan's Mitsubishi Corp and Nissho Iwai.
He said Votorantim, Gencor and Noranda were the first three companies to start viewing the CVRD information on Monday.
Borges said the minimum price for CVRD was due to be announced December 17 at the next meeting of the National Privatization Council (CND).
He said the market value of CVRD currently stood at 8-9 billion reais ($7.76-8.74 billion), but he declined to speculate on the minimum price to be set for the privatization auction.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
